verbalization: Phellandral, (R)- is proposed to interact with VMRC-MELG through a mechanistic pathway involving CDK3/Cyclin E. The evidence suggests that Phellandral, (R)- targets CDK3/Cyclin E, which is a key component of the G1 phase of the cell cycle. CDK3/Cyclin E is known to regulate cell proliferation and is a target of a specific compound, [(3S,4aS)-5-acetyloxy-6,8,10-trihydroxy-1,1,4a-trimethyl-9-oxo-7-(2-propan-2-yloxypropyl)-3,4-dihydro-2H-phenanthren-3-yl] acetate. This compound is implicated in the inhibition of VMRC-MELG, suggesting a potential mechanism of action where Phellandral, (R)- may exert its effects by modulating CDK3/Cyclin E, thereby influencing VMRC-MELG activity. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible role for Phellandral, (R)- in modulating cell cycle regulation and potentially affecting VMRC-MELG function. The evidence supports a direct, mechanistic link between Phellandral, (R)- and VMRC-MELG, emphasizing the importance of CDK3/Cyclin E in this relationship.
